1                                   III.    DEFINITIONS

2    Q.   Please identify any specialized terms that you will use in the remainder of

3         your testimony?

4    A.   For ease of reading and reference, I have defined the following terms that will be

5         used throughout my testimony:

6            •   Allocated Charges: Allocated, or indirect, charges occur when services
7                cannot be directly assigned to a specific legal entity.

 8           •   Allocating Cost Center: An Allocating Cost Center is used to collect costs
 9               that will be allocated to other Cost Centers, Internal Orders, or Work
10               Breakdown Structures (“WBS”).

11           •   Allocation Methods or Formulas: Allocation methods or formulas are the
12               basis for assigning costs to an affiliate and result from using a single
13               allocation ratio or the average of two or more allocation ratios. Examples of
14               allocation methods or formulas are: Number of Customers; Number of
15               Employees; and Assets, Revenue, and Number of Employees - known as a
16               “three-factor formula” which is based on the average of those ratios.

17           •   Allocation Ratios or Factors: Each set of allocation statistics is used to
18               calculate an allocation ratio or factor. For example, the employee ratio uses
19               the number of employees for each affiliate to the total number of employees
20               for all affiliates to determine the percentage of services chargeable to each
21               affiliate.

22           •   Allocation Statistics: Allocation statistics are the actual numerical inputs
23               used to derive the allocation ratios or factors. Examples of statistics are: the
24               number of employees, dollar amount of assets, dollar amount of revenues,
25               number of customers, number of invoice transactions, megawatt hours of
26               generation, and number of customer bills.

1    •   Assessment: The process used by the accounting system to allocate costs
2        from an allocating cost center to the receiving cost collector.

3    •   Cost Center: An organizational unit that represents a defined functional
4        location where costs are incurred.

 5   •   Cost Collector: A cost collector is a data element within the accounting
 6       system that collects costs. Cost collectors include: Internal Orders, Cost
 7       Centers, Cost Elements, and WBS Elements.

 8   •   Direct Charge: Direct charges occur when an employee of any affiliate,
 9       including XES, can clearly identify that the service being rendered is for the
10       benefit of a specific legal entity. Under XES’s accounting practices, if a
11       charge is the result of an allocation performed before the charge is entered
12       into the accounting system, then the accounting system treats the charge as
13       a direct charge. The application of an allocation performed before the
14       charge is entered into the accounting system is an “off-line allocation.”

15   •   Final Cost Center: A cost center defined by business area, Operating
16       Company or affiliate, and Profit Center.

17   •   Internal Order: Internal Orders are required for all transactions that are
18       booked into an income statement account. Each internal order is associated
19       with only one Operating Company or affiliate. All Internal Orders have
20       settlement rules assigned at the time they are created. The settlement rules
21       determine how the costs will be treated during the month-end close process
22       in SAP, the enterprise software accounting system upon which XES and the
23       Operating Companies, including SPS, rely. For example:

24       o If the settlement rule states that the costs in a specific internal order are
25         to settle by an internal order on an Operating Company or affiliate, the
26         costs are direct charged to that Operating Company or affiliate.

27       o If the settlement rule states that the costs in a specific internal order are
28         indirect or allocated Service Company charges, the Service Company
29         internal order will settle to an Allocating Cost Center in the Service

 1          Company. The Allocating Cost Center will then go through the
 2          Assessment Process to charge the costs to the appropriate legal entities.

 3   •   Labor and Labor-Related Overheads: Overhead processes are used to
 4       bill labor and labor-related overheads such as pension costs, health care
 5       costs, paid time off (e.g., vacation time, holiday, or sick time), workers’
 6       compensation, and incentive compensation (compensation is sponsored by
 7       SPS witness Tamra Newman while pension and other benefits is sponsored
 8       by SPS witness Richard R. Schrubbe).

 9   •   Legal Entity: A generic reference to an affiliate company within the Xcel
10       Energy corporate structure.

11   •   Profit Center: An SAP data element that identifies the state (e.g., New
12       Mexico) and utility (e.g., electric).

13   •   Settlement: The process used by the accounting system to move charges
14       from internal orders to the specified settlement receiver. The receiver could
15       be another internal order, an allocating cost center, or a final cost center.

16   •   Statistical Key Figures: The method by which the allocation ratios and
17       factors are organized in the accounting system and linked to allocating cost
18       centers to facilitate the performance of the assessment process to allocate
19       charges.

20   •   Work Breakdown Structures: Hierarchical cost collectors representing
21       work performed that includes various attributes to be used for the
22       reporting of costs.

3    Q.   Please describe the flow of affiliate transactions.

4    A.   To understand the flow of direct and allocated costs within the Xcel Energy

5         corporate structure, it is necessary to describe the various high-level stages that

6         costs go through in the accounting process.

7                 First, within Xcel Energy, all costs originate within an operational area and

8         a legal entity. All costs are first recorded on the books of the legal entity that is

 9        responsible for providing the service. Each accounting transaction includes detailed

10        information designating which operational area and legal entity is performing the

11        work. The accounting system also requires that an internal order be included on all

12        transactions recorded to the income statement. The internal order contains

13        information to indicate how the transaction will flow through the system. The

14        settlement rule on the internal order will indicate the legal entity to which the

15        transaction will be settled.

16                In the case of native costs described earlier in my testimony, they will

17        remain on the accounting records of the same entity. Accounting transactions for

18        native expenses are recorded directly on the books of the operating company that

 3           In the case of non-native costs incurred by one legal entity for the benefit of

 4   another entity, these costs are eventually recorded on the books of the entity

 5   receiving goods or services through the settlement and assessment processes

 6   executed within the accounting system. Every affiliate within Xcel Energy uses the

 7   same settlement and assessment processes and the same method of recording

 8   transactions. For example, if SPS personnel provided emergency storm damage

 9   assistance to PSCo, the transaction would first be recorded on SPS’s books, but the

16   billings between an Operating Company and an affiliated interest other than XES;

The following ratios will be utilized as outlined above.

       Revenue Ratio - Based on the sum of the monthly revenue amounts for the prior

       annually, or at such time as may be required due to significant changes.

       - Based on the sum of the monthly revenue amounts for the prior year ending
       December 31, the numerator of which is for an applicable Operating Company or
       affiliate company and the denominator of which is for all applicable Operating
       Companies and affiliate companies. Xcel Energy Inc. will be assigned the amount
       of intercompany dividends. This ratio will be determined annually, or at such time
       as may be required due to significant changes.

       Employee Ratio - Based on the number of employees at the end of the prior year
       ending December 31, the numerator of which is for an applicable Operating

       Operating Companies and affiliate companies. This ratio will be determined
       annually, or at such time as may be required due to significant changes

       and affiliate companies. Xcel Energy Inc. will be assigned the number of common
       officers. This ratio will be determined annually, or at such time as may be required
       due to significant changes.

       Total Assets Ratio - Based on the total assets as of December 31 for the prior year,

       and affiliate companies. This ratio will be determined annually, or at such time as
       may be required due to significant changes.
